To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the recovery of the signaling state from the receptor state is characterized by a dynamical bottleneck involving the formation of a short helix in the chromophore‐binding pocket and (2) the formation of this helix requires the chromophore to be in a trans configuration, and the helix to be stabilized by a water molecule.

(1) the formation of the photoactive signaling state in Photoactive Yellow Protein is characterized by solvent exposure of both its chromophore and a key residue, and that (2) the recovery of the signaling state to the ground‐state receptor is hindered by the formation of a transient helix in the chromophore‐binding pocket.

(i) the N‐terminus is important for the signaling state, but not for the recovery of the protein to its receptor state; (ii) the formation of the helix in the chromophore‐binding pocket is a dynamical barrier for the recovery reaction.
